genres.name: pop
genres.description: Popular music characterized by catchy melodies, strong rhythms, and broad commercial appeal. Pop songs typically feature verse-chorus structures, polished production, and themes of love, relationships, and personal experiences. Energy levels vary from upbeat dance-pop to mellow ballads.
genres.cultural_notes: Pop is designed for mass appeal and often reflects current cultural trends. It dominates streaming charts globally.

genres.name: lofi
genres.description: Lo-fi hip hop is a downtempo music genre characterized by low fidelity production, intentional imperfections, ambient textures, and nostalgic samples. It is often instrumental, featuring crackling vinyl sounds, soft piano loops, rain sounds, and mellow beats. Ideal for studying, relaxing, and background ambiance.
genres.cultural_notes: Lo-fi became synonymous with study and chill playlists on YouTube, often paired with anime aesthetics. It prioritizes mood over technical perfection.

genres.name: rock
genres.description: Rock music centers on the electric guitar, strong backbeats, and powerful vocals. It spans many subgenres from classic rock to punk to progressive rock. Rock songs often feature dynamic intensity, emotional expression, and themes of rebellion, love, and social commentary.
genres.cultural_notes: Rock has historically been associated with youth culture, rebellion, and countercultural movements. It remains one of the most influential genres in modern music history.

genres.name: ambient
genres.description: Ambient music emphasizes atmosphere and tone over traditional musical structure or rhythm. It creates immersive sonic environments using synthesizers, field recordings, and layered textures. Ambient pieces often lack beats entirely and are designed to induce calm, contemplation, or spatial awareness.
genres.cultural_notes: Ambient music is often used in spas, meditation apps, and art installations. It blurs the line between music and sound design.

genres.name: jazz
genres.description: Jazz is characterized by swing rhythms, complex harmonies, improvisation, and blue notes. It ranges from smooth jazz to bebop to fusion. Jazz emphasizes individual expression through instrumental solos and interaction between musicians. Acoustic jazz often features piano, double bass, and brushed drums.
genres.origin: Late 19th century New Orleans, African American communities
genres.cultural_notes: Jazz is considered America's classical music. It deeply influenced rock, hip-hop, and electronic music. Live improvisation makes each performance unique.

genres.name: synthwave
genres.description: Synthwave is an electronic genre inspired by 1980s film soundtracks, video game music, and pop culture. It features analog synthesizers, electronic drums, gated reverb, and nostalgic melodies. Synthwave evokes neon-lit cityscapes, cyberpunk aesthetics, and retro-futurism.
genres.cultural_notes: Synthwave gained mainstream attention through the film Drive (2011) and Stranger Things soundtrack. It represents a romanticized vision of the 1980s.

genres.name: indie pop
genres.description: Indie pop blends independent DIY aesthetics with pop sensibilities. It often features melodic hooks, jangly guitars, quirky production choices, and introspective lyrics. Unlike mainstream pop, indie pop prioritizes artistic expression and often avoids polished commercial production.
genres.cultural_notes: Indie pop thrives in local scenes and on platforms like Bandcamp. It values authenticity and often appeals to listeners seeking alternatives to mainstream radio.

genres.name: R&B
genres.description: Rhythm and Blues (R&B) combines soulful vocals with hip-hop influenced production, smooth grooves, and emotional themes. Contemporary R&B features lush harmonies, sensual melodies, and polished beats. It evolved from gospel and blues traditions into one of the most commercially successful genres.
genres.origin: 1940s African American communities, evolved from jazz and blues
genres.cultural_notes: R&B has been a dominant force in pop music since the 1990s. It often explores themes of love, heartbreak, empowerment, and sensuality.

genres.name: hip-hop
genres.description: Hip-hop is defined by rhythmic vocal delivery (rapping), beats sampled or programmed from drum machines, and lyrical storytelling. It encompasses boom-bap, trap, conscious rap, and more. Hip-hop is as much a cultural movement as a music genre, influencing fashion, language, and politics globally.
genres.cultural_notes: Hip-hop is the most consumed genre globally. It serves as a voice for marginalized communities and has shaped global youth culture for decades.

genres.name: classical
genres.description: Classical music spans a thousand years of composed instrumental and vocal music, from Gregorian chants to contemporary minimalism. It emphasizes complex structures, orchestration, and formal composition. Common forms include symphonies, concertos, sonatas, and chamber music.
genres.origin: Medieval Europe, formalized in Baroque and Classical periods
genres.cultural_notes: Classical music is foundational to Western music theory. It is frequently used in films, advertisements, and public spaces for emotional impact.

genres.name: country
genres.description: Country music tells stories of rural life, heartbreak, patriotism, and personal struggle through twangy vocals, acoustic guitars, fiddles, and steel guitars. It blends folk traditions with popular song structures. Subgenres include outlaw country, Nashville pop-country, and Americana.
genres.origin: 1920s Southern United States, Appalachian and blues traditions
genres.cultural_notes: Country music is deeply tied to American identity and rural culture. Modern country increasingly blends with pop and rock elements.

genres.name: metal
genres.description: Heavy metal is characterized by heavily distorted guitars, powerful drumming, aggressive vocals, and dark or epic themes. Subgenres include thrash, death metal, black metal, and progressive metal. Metal demands technical virtuosity and often explores complex philosophical and emotional territory.
genres.origin: Late 1960s United Kingdom and United States
genres.cultural_notes: Metal has one of the most dedicated and passionate fan communities. It is often misunderstood but offers deep musical complexity and cathartic emotional release.

genres.name: reggae
genres.description: Reggae originated in Jamaica and is defined by offbeat rhythms (skank), walking basslines, and socially conscious or spiritually uplifting lyrics. It blends Caribbean mento and calypso with American jazz and rhythm and blues. Subgenres include dub, dancehall, and roots reggae.
genres.cultural_notes: Reggae is deeply connected to Rastafarian spirituality and social justice movements. It has influenced punk, hip-hop, and electronic music worldwide.

genres.name: folk
genres.description: Folk music emphasizes acoustic instrumentation, storytelling, and traditional cultural roots. It often features fingerpicked guitars, banjos, harmonicas, and harmonies. Contemporary folk blends traditional forms with modern singer-songwriter introspection and indie aesthetics.
genres.origin: Traditional music passed orally through communities; revival in 1960s
genres.cultural_notes: Folk music preserves cultural heritage and storytelling traditions. The 1960s folk revival connected music to social and political activism.

genres.name: EDM
genres.description: Electronic Dance Music (EDM) is a broad category of electronic genres designed for clubs, festivals, and dancing. It includes house, techno, trance, and dubstep. EDM features synthesizers, drum machines, build-ups, drops, and highly produced, layered soundscapes.
genres.cultural_notes: EDM is a global cultural phenomenon centered on festivals like Tomorrowland and EDC. It emphasizes communal experiences and sensory immersion.
